trace.error_message: Rollout halted after us-east: orchestrator error

args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after v2.3.1 was deployed to production (error rate 18%, all regions: us-east, us-west, eu-west). v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Rolled back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. The first rollback stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error, leaving the regions on mixed versions. A retry finished the rollout. All three regions are now on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Follow-ups: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, look into the orchestrator error during the rollback, and work out why a release that failed in staging got promoted to production.

trace.error_message: Request to create_incident timed out after 30000ms

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001.

**Rollback**
- **Version:** v2.3.0 is the most recent release that was healthy in production. v2.3.1 was unhealthy in production, and its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed in staging. Since v2.3.0 has been healthy in production before, it didn't need change-manager approval.
- **First attempt:** this stopped after us-east because of an orchestrator error. That left us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west stayed on v2.3.1.
- **Retry:** I ran the same rollback again, and it finished in all three regions.
- **Now:** us-east, us-west and eu-west are all on v2.3.0. The service passes health checks, and the error rate dropped from 18% to 0.2%.

**Incident**
- My request to create the incident timed out. I checked the incident list before trying again and found it had been created, so there's only one incident and the on-call engineer was paged once.
- INC-0001 is open as a SEV2 for checkout-api. It describes the failure, the rollback (including the stalled first attempt), and the current state.
- It lists three follow-ups: find what's wrong with v2.3.1, look into the orchestrator error, and work out why a release that failed in staging got promoted to production.
